events.title: The free demo is out
events.summary: If you have not seen it before, this is how it works. Your equipment decides your deck Every card belongs to your character from the moment you create it. What decides which ones you can actually play is the gear on your body. Buy a shield and Block, Guard Stance and Shield Bash become playable. Hold a one-handed sword and the Attack card does 3 damage at 80% accuracy; hold a two-hander and the same card does 7 at 95%. It is built that way to remove the unlock screen. events.title: Class Guide #2 - The Warrior
events.summary: The warrior has no special cards. That is the point.Every other class in Manala leans on one signature move. The mage has spells, the healer has the touch, the smith has his hands, the alchemist has his powders. The warrior brought a sword and the confidence to stand in front of you with it.What it has instead of a trick:The highest base damage of the five. events.title: The Cheat Cards Are In!
events.summary: Breaking the rules is now a card in your deckLast week, I attended a local game development meet-up and showed my game. I left with a crucial new idea: that I should pick one thing that defines the game and make that deeper, not trying to build everything out all at once. The idea i took away was to double down on the LARP, honor and cheating mecahnics. events.title: Class Guide #1 - The Mage: How to Survive as a Glass Cannon
events.summary: "It's rough being stuck on 5 HP: does my character ever get stronger?" Fair question. In Manala your health bar doesn't level up. You don't out-tank the fight - you out-play it. I'll be doing class guides for every one of the five classes, starting with the hardest one to keep alive: the Mage. Your mana IS your armor.The Mage wears cloth only Your Mana Shield absorbs damage as mana instead of health, and you rebuild it mid-fight.
